agent_final_answer:
The most popular Quantum Physics news in the past month (Quantum Physics topic, sorted by Popular -> 1 month) is "Cutting a photon in two creates an infinite swarm of particles" (Phys.org, Jun 2, 2026). It has 20 comments:

1. Lino Di Ischia (20h ago, score -4): This is an absurd result indicating that something is seriously wrong with the 'theory.' But, of course, we already know something is wrong with the theory because it leads to an error of 10^120.
2. Elmo_McGillicutty (20h, -4): A photon is not a particle. It has a discreet duration and density which gives it some torque momentum. It measures like a particle. But it has no mass. No substance. It's field only... For a "photon" is only 1/2 wavelength long physically (fly by time), and has a 1/2 period duration. It's the field skin of an expanding c speed sphere with a handed density gradient.
3. Elmo_McGillicutty (20h, -4): Light (electric fields) spreads and diverges at an inverse square rate. If we can see 13 billion old light, what does that tell us? It tells us that the field "line" substance of the electric is very dense and very fine.
4. RapidLaser6754 (19h, 0): I hate to say it, but this just killed all credibility I have for this page. This is being made out to be a "huge" revelation, when in actual science "infinity" or zeroes literally mean that there's a concept hidden we don't understand yet.
5. Elmo_McGillicutty (18h, -4): I believe infinity and zero is possible, but no way to confirm it. Infinity by definition can not be observed or measured... Recent coatings will block all EM fields and radiation... the interior should be zero. Void of mass and field. And no CMBR. A cold quiet spot.
6. Hermitian (17h, 0): "Infinite" -- whether countably many or real-number infinity, is incorrect. "Intractable" would have been a better choice of words.
7. Mark1000 (16h, -3): Hey RapidLaser6754, you have certainly surprised me today... 'Photons' don't actually exist - that is just the name for light quanta, which do exist, but which physicists don't fully understand so they surrender their intellect to abstract QM equations.
8. goldeneye (16h, -2): Energy is proportional to its Subdivision. A Photon's energy is contained within one oscillation. So subdividing one oscillation subdivides the Photon into unlimited numbers of Photon's... What you're seeing is not what you're actually seeing.
9. PhysicsPhD (15h, 2): Remember the reshaped photon wave packet due to negative group delay in a material medium? That's this case...and there is no "cutting the particle" or "infinite swarms". Flawed gedanken experiment.
10. out of bounds (15h, 2): Mark1000, that is perhaps the most ridiculous statement you've made yet... As they mean identical concepts, most of us prefer "photon" over "light quantum" - easier to write, easier to say.
11. Raffjake (13h, -1): Seem like there is a lot of gravity between this and supercritical co2 states.
12. Batta1890 (11h, 0): Strange...Analysis of an impossible scenario. And surprise, the result is bizarre and meaningless. Why not analyze what happens if you chop an electron in half?
13. SBKaravashkin (10h, -2): ...we already know something is wrong with the theory because it leads to an error of 10^120... back in the 19th century Fresnel proved the absurdity of the corpuscular concept... dividing the photon into two should result in frequency separation.
14. SBKaravashkin (10h, 0): Good question. Then they can "cut" both quarks and neutrinos. To cut is to cut. :-D
15. DaveKorn (4h, 0): No. The size of a wavepacket is inversely related to the spread of frequencies that compose it... This situation is pretty similar to quark confinement... with the minor difference that photons are their own antiparticle.
16. MauroIT (3h, -1): A shutter that splits a photon in two would have to have infinite speed... it would generate a variation in the electric field with duration 0... with equivalent components at all frequencies from 0 to infinite Hz.
17. SBKaravashkin (2h, -1): I don't understand this crowd that immorally distorts physics... Is a photon a wave train? What spectrum does this wave train have, how thick is it?... The photonists are clearly possessed by some sick imagination.
18. goldeneye (2h, -1): What Albert discovered which he received a Nobel for... An electron won't accept subdivisions of a cycle, it has to be a complete cycle, or not at all.
19. SBKaravashkin (1h, -1): If you lifted a weight, you expended a certain amount of energy. Does this mean that this energy became discrete, acquired a frequency, and flew away from you as a materialized object? :-)
20. Mark1000 (1h, -1): I wonder if "professor" out of bounds can describe to us the actual shape and size of these alleged photons... how a CLAIM that something can exist in TWO different states simultaneously, but is ONLY ever measured being in ONE state, is an actual scientific claim?
